title: Dual-responsive poly( N -isopropylacrylamide- co -methacrylic acid) hydrogels: role and synergies of pH and temperature in tailoring hydrogel responsiveness
content: Stimuli–responsive hydrogels based on poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-methacrylic acid) (P(NIPAMm-co-MAAn)) have well-established dual pH- and thermoresponsive behaviour. Here, we investigate how a relatively low MAA content (10, 20, or 30 mol%) impacts on the physicochemical properties and coupled thermo- and pH-responsive behaviour, bringing pH dominance over temperature. Crosslinked P(NIPAMm-co-MAAn) hydrogels were synthesised by photopolymerization from varying proportions of the thermoresponsive monomer NIPAM and the pH-responsive monomer MAA (10, 20, or 30 mol% MAA), using 1 mol% N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide (BIS) as crosslinker. Swelling, compressive elastic modulus, water contact angle, pore size, transition temperature, and enthalpy of phase transition were studied as a function of temperature and pH for the P(NIPAMm-co-MAAn) hydrogels. The pH-dependent behaviour of the thermoresponsive copolymer hydrogels is attributed to hydrogen bonding interactions between NIPAM and MAA units, predominant at low pH, and to the enhanced hydration of ionised MAA carboxylate groups at high pH. Although the MAA content did not exceed 30 mol%, it played a key role in determining hydrogel properties. Notably, pH had a stronger effect than temperature on hydrogel responsiveness, and at high pH, hydrogels largely lose their ability to undergo volume collapse above the volume phase transition temperature (VPTT).
